scope: A quantitative recurrence for the actual one-coordinate Gibbs marginal: c_new(i,j)=c(i,j)+c(i,e)*c(e,j) on distinct retained coordinates, with zero eliminated row/column and diagonal. The coefficient bounds one quarter of every mixed action rectangle. Exact logarithmic integration proves the new mixed bound. A nonnegative symmetric zero-diagonal matrix with row sums <=alpha<=1 preserves that same row budget after every finite stage of genuine coordinate elimination. For actual SU(2) Wilson input this supplies the depth- and volume-independent bound 36*beta when 0<=beta<=1/36, and discharges generated-action smallness for the auxiliary contraction criterion in the strict small-beta regime. Uniform control of the coloring, entry from beta(a)->infinity, physical-time decay, nontrivial continuum limit and physical mass gap remain unproved.
normalization: MixedBound(A,c) means every mixed action rectangle in coordinates i,j is bounded by 4*c(i,j); hence c bounds actual single-coordinate conditional influence.

one_step.operator: The existing GibbsCoordinateElimination.blockAction on the singleton {e}; its equality to -log integral exp(-A(update(U,e,q))) dmu(q) is proved.
one_step.recurrence: For i,j distinct and different from e, c_new(i,j)=c(i,j)+c(i,e)*c(e,j). The diagonal and eliminated row/column are zero.
one_step.derivation: The pre-existing mixed term contributes 4*c(i,j). The oscillations of the two boundary action changes in the integrated variable are bounded by 4*c(e,i) and 4*c(e,j). The actual free-energy rectangle estimate contributes their product divided by four. Symmetry yields the stated normalized recurrence.
one_step.row_accounting: sum_j c_new(i,j) <= sum_j c(i,j)-c(i,e)+c(i,e)*sum_j c(e,j) <= alpha-(1-alpha)*c(i,e) <= alpha when alpha<=1.
one_step.no_independence_assumption: One coordinate is genuinely integrated at each step. Arbitrary schedules, including repeated choices, are covered; no conditional product law for a larger block is assumed.

iteration.result: Every finite action in the actual GibbsCoordinateTower for singleton schedules has the recursively computed mixed bound. Nonnegativity, symmetry, zero diagonal and the initial row budget persist.
iteration.wilson_application: Actual SU(2) plaquette oscillations provide the seed matrix. For 0<=beta<=1/36, every finite induced Wilson action has row budget at most 36*beta, independent of lattice volume and elimination depth.
iteration.contraction: For beta<1/36, the generated-factor auxiliary L2 contraction now follows from the initial beta condition and any valid current-support coloring. The former per-stage smallness premise is discharged in this regime. The rate still depends on the color count.
iteration.improvement_over_global_weights: The proof estimates mixed variations of the sum of actual generated factors, retaining cancellations that separate global factor-amplitude bounds lose.

limitations: This is stability inside an already established small-influence regime, not entry into it from the weak-coupling limit beta->infinity.
The theorem is for exact one-site coordinate elimination. No identification with Balaban gauge-covariant block averaging is asserted.
The row bound does not control the number of colors needed for enlarged interaction supports or the physical-time propagation of observables.
Elimination may increase individual retained couplings even while the total row bound remains controlled.
No nontrivial continuum correlation limit, source-uniform bound, finite physical-energy witness or physical mass gap is proved.
remaining: Prove entry into a small coarse mixed-interaction budget along a physically justified weak-coupling cutoff trajectory; the stability theorem starts from a budget <=1 and does not establish crossover.
Control actual large-field, boundary and source contributions uniformly after background cancellation; relate the exact coordinate-elimination construction to a physical-scale coarse representation.
Control a valid current-support coloring uniformly or prove physical clustering directly from a weighted influence matrix; row-budget stability alone does not give a volume-uniform color-update rate.
Prove the original transfer fixed-physical-slab estimate and construct nontrivial continuum correlations with a nonzero finite-energy excitation on the same trajectory.
All twelve full Clay obligations remain open.
